## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.

### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`

The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.

`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`

```yaml
# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
validate:
  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
  next: load
load:
  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
  next: apply
apply:
  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
```

```java
// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
public class ValidateOwner {
  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
  }
}
public class LoadOwner {
  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
    ownerOut.set(owner);
  }
}
public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
  }
}
public class SaveOwner {
  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
    repository.save(owner);
  }
}
public class RespondWithOwner {
  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
  }
}
```

```java
public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,

  }
}
```

### Step wiring

Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
`method:`.

- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
  as `@Parameter T`.
- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
  branch; not calling it short-circuits.

### Function parameters

Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:

- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`

Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.

public class ApplyPerson {
    public void apply(@Val PersonRequest request, @Val Person person, SheetRepository sheets, Out<Person> updated)
            throws StalePersonException {
        if (request.version() != null && request.version() != person.version()) {
            throw new StalePersonException(person.name());

        boolean blank = request.gradeFrom() == null || request.gradeFrom().isEmpty();
        if (blank && request.grade().equals(person.grade())) {

        LocalDate today = sheets.today(person.sheetId());

        updated.set(person.withNameAndGrade(request.name(), request.grade(), from, today));

I read the code and changed nothing. Every figure on screen is worked out in the browser (TypeScript, mostly `features/rates/rates.ts`). The server (Java) works the same figures out again for settling, statements, closing periods and the audit file.

## 1. Figures and the rules behind them

### Claim row
| testid | What it shows / rule |
|---|---|
| `claim-amount`, `claim-date`, `claim-note` | As stored. A blank date means the sheet's `today` (`BuildClaim`, `ApplyClaim`). |
| `claim-status` | `ClaimStatus`: DRAFT → OPEN → SETTLED. A clerk's settle can make it PENDING instead; PENDING goes to SETTLED (approve) or back to OPEN (reject). DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING can go to VOID. SETTLED and VOID are final, except that a steward can **RESETTLE** a SETTLED claim. Allowed moves are in `ClaimAction.allowedFrom`. |
| `claim-number` | Given on **open** (`ApplyClaimAction.nextNumber`). Normally it is the sheet-wide `nextClaimNumber` (1, 2, …). When `periodNumberingFrom` is set and `today` is on or after it, it is `<period>-n` for the period that contains the claim's date, or `X-n` if no period does (`nextPeriodClaimNumber`). A number is never reused, and a voided claim keeps its number. |
| `claim-opened-by` | The user who opened it. |
| `claim-due-by` | `dueBy` = date + `termsFor(gradeOn(date), date)`: the grade's own terms in force on that date, else the sheet's terms (14 to start). Fixed when the claim is **created**; editing the date or terms later doesn't change it. |
| `claim-due` | `claimDue` / `Claim.due` (detail below). |
| `claim-overdue` | `overdue`: OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `dueBy < today`. |
| `claim-deferred`, `-until` | `deferred`: OPEN and `today < deferredUntil`. |
| `claim-stated` | The person's last statement bound this claim. |
| `claim-corrects` | For a correction, the number of the claim it corrects. |
| `claim-period` | `periodOf`: the period whose dates contain the claim's date. |
| `claim-log-line` | `LogClaimStatus`: status, user, `today`, and the due at that moment (`ClaimDueNow`). |

**How a claim's due is worked out** (`Claim.figure` / `Claim.due`, `LateCharge`, `Rounding`; in TS `claimFigure` / `claimDue` / `lateCharge`):
1. If it has a fixed `due` (settled), show that. It already includes any late charge.
2. Otherwise, if it is `bound()` (stated and not PENDING), the figure is `statedDue`.
3. Otherwise it is **live**: amount × `Rate.inForce(rates, gradeOn(claim.date), claim.date)` / 100, rounded to 2 decimals.
   - A rate is in force from its latest from-date on or before the date. It stops at its to-date. With no rate in force the due is **n/a**.
   - The result is raised to `floorOn(claim.date)` (the floor starts at 1.00). **A correction has no floor.**
4. Then the late charge is added: `latePctOn(claim.date)` × number of full 30-day periods past `dueBy`, applied to the figure and rounded the same way.
   - Only OPEN or PENDING claims are charged; deferred claims and corrections never are.
   - The late charge is **never bound** by a statement. It keeps following `today` until the claim is settled.
5. **Rounding** (`Rounding.modeFor`): half-up if the claim's date is before `policyDate`, half-even on or after it.
   - A blank `policyDate` means **today**, so the rounding mode can change as `today` moves.
   - A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects.

### Person row
- **`person-claimed`** (`claimed`): the sum of amounts of the claims that count.
  - `counts` / `Person.counts`: SETTLED always counts. OPEN or PENDING counts unless it is deferred, or a **hold** covers its date and it is not bound.
  - DRAFT and VOID never count.
- **`person-due-total`** (`personDue` / `RollupService`): the sum of the counting claims' dues (n/a skipped), then capped at `capOn(today)`.
  - It is **n/a** when the person's grade on `today` has no rate on `today` *and* no counting claim has a figure (`keepsFigure`, or a live figure from its own date's rate).
- **`person-excess`**: by how much the uncapped sum is above the cap (0.00 if not above, or if n/a).
- **`person-overdue-count` / `-total`** (`personOverdue`): the counting claims that are overdue, and their dues added up. Not capped.
- **`person-period-<name>-due-total`** (`personPeriodDue`): live dues of counting claims dated in the period. Once the period is **closed**, the value is the frozen `personTotals` (0.00 for anyone added since).
- **`person-backing`**: the person's patrons' due-totals added up, n/a skipped.
- **`person-statement-count` / `stated-total` / `statement-date`** (`TakeStatement`):
  - The statement binds every counting claim to its figure at that moment, and unbinds every other claim.
  - It records the due-total (capped, same n/a rule) and `today`.
- **`person-grade`**: the grade in force on `today`. An edit records a grade from its from-date (blank means today) and replaces any grade recorded for that same date. Saving the same grade with a blank date records nothing (`ApplyPerson`).
- **`person-retired` / `-from`, `person-hold` / `-hold-line`**:
  - Holds can only be added; there is no release. A blank from-date means today, and the to-date must not be before the from-date.
  - Retired people's claims still count.

### Sheet-wide figures
- `rollup-claimed-total`, `rollup-due-total` (n/a people skipped), `rollup-overdue-count` / `-total`.
- `header-*`: the people count includes retired people, plus claim counts per status.
- `summary-grade-*`: excludes retired people and groups by today's grade.
- `summary-period-*` and `period-due-total`.
- `rate-current-<g>`.
- The server repeats claimed, due-total and overdue-total in its `ROLLUP` / `TOTALS` audit lines (`AuditRollup`).

### Freezing
- **Settle and approve** freeze the due as it is at that moment, late charge included (`ClaimDueNow`). If there is no rate the due stays live.
  - A claim bound by a statement settles at the bound figure.
  - A clerk whose due is above `clerkLimitOn(today)` gets **PENDING** instead. A due of n/a is within any limit.
- **Approve** fixes the live figure at the moment of approval. While PENDING the claim is unbound; a reject makes it bound again.
- **Resettle** re-fixes the claim as if it were an open, unbound claim on today's rates. The old due goes into the audit.
- **Statement** binds figures, but not the late charge. A reassign unbinds the claim.
- **Close period** freezes the period total and each person's total. Individual claims are *not* frozen.

### What dates decide
- The claim's **date** picks the grade, rate, floor, late %, terms (and so `dueBy`), rounding mode and period.
- **`today`** decides:
  - overdue status and late periods
  - deferral
  - the cap and clerk limit in force
  - the grade used for the n/a test
  - default dates
  - when period numbering starts
- **Dated settings** (`DatedSettings`) use the value with the latest from-date on or before the date.
  - Blank floor, terms or late % reset to 1.00, 14 or 0.00.
  - Blank cap or clerk limit means none.
  - A field that wasn't touched is left as it is.

### Who may do what, and what's refused
- **Steward only:** approve, reject (a reason is required), resettle, move a claim to another person (`CheckClaimReassign`), and reopen a period.
- **Four eyes:** the user who opened a claim can't settle or approve it.
- **Anyone at all can:** set roles (so anyone can make themselves a steward), change settings and rates, close a period, take a statement, hold, retire, defer, void, open and edit.
- **Edits:** only a DRAFT can be edited (`CheckClaimDraft`).
- **Deferral:** only an OPEN claim, to a date after today. A deferred claim can't be settled.
- **Corrections:** a negative amount must name a SETTLED claim of the same person.
- **Retirement:** a claim dated *after* `retiredFrom` is refused. A claim on the retirement date itself is allowed. A move to a retired person is refused the same way.
- **Closed period:**
  - Refuses adding or editing a claim to a date inside it.
  - Refuses *any* action (status change, defer, move) on a claim dated inside it.
  - Does **not** stop rate, setting, grade, hold or statement changes. Those still move person totals, but not the frozen period figures.
- **Paste ("import")** (`ValidatePasteRequest` / `FindPastedPeople`):
  - It is all-or-nothing. Each line goes through the claim form's checks, plus the retirement and closed-period checks.
  - Names are matched ignoring case.
  - Negative amounts are refused.
  - It adds DRAFT claims and returns the count added.
- **Quick-add:** an unknown name creates a person with grade A, and the claim is dated today. If the claim is refused, the person isn't added.
- **Concurrent edits:** a person edit made from an old `version` is refused (409).

### Inconsistencies I noticed
1. **Corrections can round differently.** Rounding a correction needs the date of the claim it corrects. `ClaimDueNow` and `TakeStatement` look that date up among the person's own claims only. `RollupService` and the browser look across the whole sheet. If the corrected claim has been moved to someone else, a correction's settled, logged or stated figure can be rounded differently from what the screen shows.
2. **Claim numbers can repeat.** A period named `X` and the no-period sequence both produce `X-1`, `X-2`, … from separate counters, so two claims can get the same number.

## 2. How hard it was to follow

It was hard. The rules are not in one place:
- Each one is split across dozens of single-step Java classes, wired together in YAML, so you only see the order of checks by reading the YAML files.
- The money logic exists twice: once in Java (`Claim`, `LateCharge`, `Rounding`, `RollupService`, `TakeStatement`, `ClosePeriod`) and once in TypeScript (`rates.ts`, `claims.ts`, `dueBy.ts`, `periods.ts`, `settings.ts`). The two must be kept in step by hand.

What saves it is that the doc comments are thorough and state each rule in plain words. Even so, a new developer would need several hours, and would have to compare both copies to trust either.
